{"rule": "Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.", "text": "The path to the slip was steeper than she remembered, or she was slower. Either way she took it with a hand on the bramble stems, not minding the scratches, watching her feet and not the water. The wind had gone round to the north while she made tea. It brought the smell of weed and cold stone and nothing else.

The posts were closer together than they looked from the window. Between them the mud had begun to show, dark and shining, pocked where the water still drained from it. Gulls stood about on it in the way gulls do, as if they had been posted there and forgotten.

She saw the marks before she reached the bottom. A keel had come in on the last of the flood and gone out again on the first of the ebb, a long clean furrow with a scatter of footprints beside it. One set. Boots, not large. They went up the slip toward the house and came back down, and the ones coming back were spaced wider, as if whoever made them had been in less of a hurry.

She stood at the top of the furrow and looked out. The channel was empty to the point. Beyond the point the sea was the flat grey of a thing that had nothing to say.

So they had come, and left the chart, and gone. No word. No knock. Just the door unbarred, the way you leave a door for someone you expect to follow.

She found she was not afraid. She was, of all things, insulted."}
